ei.subject: 수능특강Light 영어
ei.title: I remember the day my first book came out.

fullPassage: I remember the day my first book came out. The week before, I talked to people around me almost every day about how excited I was, how long I had waited, and how it felt just like being a little kid waiting for Christmas Eve. Finally, the big day arrived and I woke up happy, already embarrassed by all the praise and attention I thought would come. I made coffee and waited for someone to call and congratulate me. But the phone didn't know its part. It sat there silent as death with a head cold. By noon, the silence was getting on my nerves. I sat by the phone like a loyal dog. Finally, it rang at four. I picked it up — only to hear someone asking for someone else. I kept glancing at the phone for hours, but it never rang again. The day ended in silence, and so did my excitement.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 출간되다(came out), 흥분한(excited), 행복한(happy).
det.analysis:
✅ ① came out — excited — happy: 책이 '출간된' 날, '흥분한' 상태로 매일 이야기했고, '행복하게' 일어났다는 문맥에 적합.
❌ ② fell apart — excited — happy: fell apart(무너진)는 출간과 반대.
❌ ③ came out — bored — happy: bored(지루한)는 크리스마스 이브를 기다리는 흥분과 반대.
❌ ④ came out — excited — miserable: miserable(비참한)은 행복한 아침과 반대.
det.tip: come out = 출간되다 ↔ fall apart, excited ↔ bored, happy ↔ miserable

questions.passage: I remember the day my first book came out. The week before, I talked to people around me almost every day about how excited I was, how long I had waited, and how it felt just like being a little kid waiting for Christmas Eve. Finally, the big day arrived and I woke up happy, already embarrassed by all the (A)[criticism / praise] and attention I thought would come. I made coffee and waited for someone to call and (B)[insult / congratulate] me. But the phone didn't know its part. It sat there silent as death with a head cold. By noon, the silence was getting on my (C)[feet / nerves]. I sat by the phone like a loyal dog. Finally, it rang at four. I picked it up — only to hear someone asking for someone else. I kept glancing at the phone for hours, but it never rang again. The day ended in silence, and so did my excitement.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 칭찬(praise), 축하하다(congratulate), 신경(nerves).
det.analysis:
✅ ② praise — congratulate — nerves: '칭찬'과 관심을 받을 것으로 예상했고, 누군가 '축하해 주길' 기다렸으며, 침묵이 '신경'을 건드렸다는 문맥에 적합.
❌ ① criticism — congratulate — nerves: criticism(비판)은 쑥스러움/기대와 반대.
❌ ③ praise — insult — nerves: insult(모욕하다)는 축하 상황과 반대.
❌ ④ praise — congratulate — feet: get on one's feet는 숙어이지만 여기선 get on one's nerves(신경 건드리다)가 맞음.
det.tip: praise ↔ criticism, congratulate ↔ insult, get on one's nerves = 신경을 건드리다

questions.passage: I remember the day my first book came out. questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 충성스러운(loyal), 힐끗 보는(glancing), 침묵(silence).
det.analysis:
✅ ③ loyal — glancing — silence: '충성스러운' 개처럼 전화기 옆에 앉아, 전화기를 '힐끗' 보며, '침묵'으로 하루가 끝났다는 문맥에 적합.
❌ ① disloyal — glancing — silence: disloyal(불충한)은 곁에 앉아 기다리는 모습과 반대.
❌ ② loyal — ignoring — silence: ignoring(무시하는)은 계속 쳐다본 행동과 반대.
❌ ④ loyal — glancing — applause: applause(박수)는 침묵 상황과 반대.
det.tip: loyal ↔ disloyal, glance at = 힐끗 보다, silence ↔ applause

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ punishment(처벌) → attention(관심). 책 출간 축하로 '관심'을 받을 것이라 예상한 문맥이므로 punishment는 부적절.
det.analysis:
✅ ① excited: 흥분한 → 적절
✅ ② happy: 행복한 → 적절
✅ ③ praise: 칭찬 → 적절
❌ ④ punishment → attention: 관심이 원문. 처벌은 문맥 무관.
det.tip: attention(관심) = interest, notice. ↔ punishment(처벌)

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ same(같은) → else(다른). 전화를 받았더니 '다른' 사람을 찾는 소리였다는 문맥.
det.analysis:
✅ ① congratulate: 축하하다 → 적절
✅ ② silent: 조용한 → 적절
❌ ③ same → else: asking for someone else(다른 사람을 찾는)가 원문. 'same'은 '같은'이므로 반대.
✅ ④ loyal: 충성스러운 → 적절
det.tip: someone else = 다른 누군가. asking for someone else = 다른 사람을 찾는

det.korean: ④ didn't → did. 'so did my excitement'는 '내 설렘도 역시 끝났다'는 so 도치 구문으로 긍정형 did가 와야 합니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① woke up: 일어났다 → 적절
✅ ② getting: get on one's nerves → 적절
✅ ③ glancing: 힐끗 보는 → 적절
❌ ④ didn't → did: so + 동사 + 주어 = ~도 역시 그렇다. The day ended in silence, and so did my excitement(내 설렘도 끝났다). 긍정 도치이므로 didn't(부정)는 부적절.
det.tip: so + 조동사 + 주어 = ~도 역시. The day ended, and so did my excitement = 하루가 끝났고, 내 설렘도 (끝났다)
